page.layout: One page of running text in a single column. Running head at the top, page number at the top right. Two short marginal notes at the lower right, beside the last lines. No text in the left margin.

main_text.p: ostra peccata, quæ ut Sponsor in se susceperat, expiaverit, pròq; illis judicio Dei satisfecerit. 1. Corint. 15. 17. Si Christus non est excitatus, inanis est fides vestra; adhuc estis in peccatis vestris.

Ergò cum Christus sit excitatus, se-quitur credentes non amplius esse in peccatis suis, nec fidem eorum inanem esse; nempe fidem, quâ credunt peccata sua per mortem Christi esse expiata. Roman. 4. v. ult. Qui (nempe Jesus) traditus est propter delicta nostra (scilicet exp-iandos suâ morte) & excitatus est propter iustificationem nostri (scilicet testificandam, quòd nimirum illa facta sit per sanguinem ipsius. Confer cap. 5. 9.) Actor.13. postquam Apostolus ex Psal. 18. osten-disset, Jesum esse Christum, ut qui incorruptus excitatus sit à mortuis, subjungit: Notum ergo sit vobis, fratres, quòd per hunc vobis remissio peccatorum annunciatur. Huc pertinet quòd Petrus dicit: Bonam conscientiam Deum interrogare per resurrectionem Jesu Christi, de quo dicto supra satis.
3. Si daretur, inquiunt, CHRISTUM semel se mortem æternam pro nobis, non tamen esset [?].

page.notes: Marginal notes at lower right, cut off and partly illegible: "aliud sophis-ta specio-sum de sa-" (approximate reading; the second and third lines are very faint). The last line of text ends at the right edge with a partly hidden word, and the end of "effet" is uncertain. The word after "suscēperat" is partly cut off at the line end; "susceperat" is read from the image. "semel" in the last line is a guess and is not clearly printed. Italics in the Scripture quotations are read from the scan.
